stemMd: A sound wave travels through air. Which description is correct?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Air particles travel from the source to the listener at the wave speed.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Air particles oscillate only perpendicular to the propagation direction.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Air particles oscillate mainly parallel to the direction of wave propagation.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Sound in air is an electromagnetic wave.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Sound can propagate through a perfect vacuum as pressure variations.

explanationMd: Ordinary sound in air is longitudinal: local compressions and rarefactions move through the medium while particles oscillate back and forth approximately along the propagation direction. Energy travels with the wave; individual air particles do not travel all the way from source to receiver.

distractorRationale.a: Particles oscillate locally rather than moving with the wave over that distance.
distractorRationale.d: Sound is a mechanical pressure wave requiring a medium.
distractorRationale.b: That describes transverse rather than ordinary longitudinal sound in air.
distractorRationale.e: A vacuum has no material medium to carry pressure variations.
